question_text:
A 54-year-old man with lymphoma presents to his oncologist with severe abdominal pain and flank pain. He says that the pain started 2 days ago and has gotten worse over time. He has also not been able to urinate over the same time period. On presentation, his temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 110/72 mmHg, pulse is 105/min, and respirations are 12/min. Physical exam reveals bilateral flank tenderness. Labs results are shown below:

Blood urea nitrogen: 34 mg/dL
Creatinine: 3.7 mg/dl
Urine osmolality: 228 mOsm/kg

Renal ultrasonography shows dilation of the kidneys bilaterally with a normal-sized bladder. Which of the following would most likely be beneficial in treating this patient's condition?

                    ### Question
                    A 54-year-old man with lymphoma presents to his oncologist with severe abdominal pain and flank pain. He says that the pain started 2 days ago and has gotten worse over time. He has also not been able to urinate over the same time period. On presentation, his temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 110/72 mmHg, pulse is 105/min, and respirations are 12/min. Physical exam reveals bilateral flank tenderness. Labs results are shown below:

Blood urea nitrogen: 34 mg/dL
Creatinine: 3.7 mg/dl
Urine osmolality: 228 mOsm/kg

Renal ultrasonography shows dilation of the kidneys bilaterally with a normal-sized bladder. Which of the following would most likely be beneficial in treating this patient's condition?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Administration of a loop diuretic
opb. Bilateral stenting of the renal arteries
opc. Bilateral stenting of the ureters
opd. Catheterization of the bladder
ope. Volume repletion with saline

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's presentation of severe abdominal and flank pain, inability to urinate, elevated creatinine and BUN levels, and bilateral kidney dilation on ultrasonography suggests acute obstructive uropathy, likely due to ureteral obstruction from lymphoma-related lymph node enlargement. The consensus in medical practice supports that in cases of obstructive uropathy causing renal failure, the primary treatment is to relieve the obstruction. Bilateral stenting of the ureters is indicated to restore urine flow and alleviate kidney pressure, as supported by the evidence paths linking kidney and urinary tract obstruction to pathological dilatation and disease manifestations. Other options like loop diuretics, catheterization of the bladder, or volume repletion with saline do not directly address the underlying obstruction and are therefore not suitable as primary interventions in this context.
